title: 2026 HSE permit eligibility and conversion QA

sources.publisher: Environment Agency and Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
sources.title: UK Emissions Trading Scheme for hospital or small emitters: how to comply

sources.publisher: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
sources.title: Participating in the UK ETS

facts.source_fact: An HSE permit can only be held where the installation has HSE status for the relevant allocation period.
facts.expected_handling: Require relevant-period HSE status before HSE permit.

facts.source_fact: A GHGE permit holder that is HSE for 2026–2030 is converted by the regulator to an HSE permit effective 1 January 2026.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve regulator conversion and effective date.

facts.source_fact: A USE that loses eligibility may apply for an HSE permit on regulator advice.
facts.expected_handling: Do not infer automatic HSE entry from USE exit.

facts.source_fact: A new HSE permit application is made using METS.
The regulator issues the HSE permit only after approving the application.
facts.expected_handling: Do not treat application as approval.

facts.source_fact: The permit includes conditions to monitor and report emissions and notify the regulator of changes.
HSEs report annual emissions but use emissions targets rather than surrendering allowances.
facts.expected_handling: Keep HSE target regime separate from main-scheme surrender.

facts.source_fact: HSEs are not entitled to free allocation while under HSE status.
facts.expected_handling: Do not assign free allocation to HSE status.

facts.source_fact: An installation primarily serving a hospital can qualify where at least 85% of produced heat is used by or supplied to hospitals, subject to period criteria.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve hospital-service threshold and period criteria.

facts.source_fact: A non-hospital small emitter must meet emissions and, where applicable, thermal-input criteria for the relevant allocation period.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve eligibility criteria without inferring status from one metric.
